name: HubSpot
note: Docs: two ways to authenticate, OAuth and private app access tokens. Private apps need a super admin in the HubSpot account. Docs fetched do not say 'free account', so access is medium confidence.

name: Twenty
note: API key created in Settings. OAuth supported. Official MCP page in Twenty docs. Open source, so self-hosting is possible. 'Free' is inferred from open source, not quoted.

name: DealCloud
note: OAuth2 client credentials (client id + secret). Credentials come from an admin enabling the API key inside a customer's own DealCloud site, so you need an existing tenant. No public free signup found. Official MCP docs on the same docs site. Last link is third party.

name: Zendesk
note: API tokens use Basic auth; OAuth access tokens also supported. Both methods are off by default in new accounts until an admin enables them. API tokens are being deactivated on 2027-04-30, OAuth is the way forward. MCP not checked.

name: Slack
note: OAuth 2.0 installs give bearer tokens (bot, user, app). Official Slack MCP server exists but only for Marketplace-published or internal apps. 'Free' not quoted in the pages fetched.

name: WhatsApp Business
note: Graph API calls use access tokens; permanent token from a system user. Accessing WABAs you do not own needs Advanced access through App Review. Developer can start with a test number self-serve. MCP not checked.

name: Google Ads
note: OAuth2 plus a developer-token style access level. Test and Explorer levels are quick; Basic and Standard need application review. Page says developer tokens were sunset 2026-09-09 and access levels moved to Cloud projects. Only gRPC is quoted on the page; REST is from general knowledge. Google page mentions a published Google Ads MCP server.

name: Shopify
note: GraphQL Admin API uses OAuth (usually token exchange). New custom apps go through the Dev Dashboard with OAuth. Partner account being free is from a third-party guide (apideck.com). REST Admin API is legacy, so graphql only here.

name: Amazon Selling Partner
note: Login with Amazon (OAuth 2.0). You must register as an SP-API developer and Amazon decides on the profile. Public apps must be listed in the Selling Partner Appstore, which needs Amazon approval. Private apps need a professional seller account. REST is from general knowledge.

name: fanbasis
note: CORRECTED after human spot-check. Official API docs live at commasdocs.com (Commas, fanbasis API brand), base URL fanbasis.com/public-api. Auth is x-api-key header; key made in dashboard under Account > API Keys. Free signup cost not verified (seller account needed). Original label (no_public_api) was wrong because the agent-independent search never found this docs domain.

name: DataForSEO
note: Docs: Basic authentication is the only way to access the API. Free account with $1 trial credit and a free sandbox. Docs landing page says REST.

name: Sherlock
note: Open-source CLI installed with pipx/pip/docker. Not a hosted API, no auth. A toolkit would need to run it locally or in a sandbox.

name: Waterfall.io
note: Only third-party pages found (One, Cargo). They show x-api-key header and https://api.waterfall.io/v1 endpoints. No official docs page retrieved and no clear statement on how to get a key. LOW confidence: human must check waterfall.io directly.

name: GitHub
note: REST docs list personal access tokens, GitHub Apps and OAuth. Official GitHub MCP server repo. 'Free' and GraphQL are from general knowledge, not quoted on the pages fetched.

name: Notion
note: Internal connections use an API token, public connections use OAuth 2.0. Page does not say whether credentials are free, and does not mention MCP, so both are not verified.

name: Stripe
note: API is REST, key decides live vs sandbox, sandboxes need no live data. MCP page: official server at mcp.stripe.com with OAuth or agent API keys.

name: iPayX
note: Page describes an FX audit web flow. It does not mention auth, endpoints or developer credentials. Only a meta keyword 'MCP FX server'. LOW confidence: human should check the Pricing and About pages.

name: PitchBook
note: PitchBook help page: API is separate from the platform and needs a standalone contract, access set up with their team via API key or token. Frontegg page (third party) gives header format 'PB-Token' and says no free tier.

name: NotebookLM
note: API is part of NotebookLM Enterprise: needs a Google Cloud project with billing, identity setup, a subscription and user licenses. OAuth2 and REST are inferred from it being a Google Cloud API, not quoted.

name: Mermaid CLI
note: Command-line tool that turns mermaid files into SVG/PNG/PDF. No auth or account. Has a Node.js API but README says it is not covered by semver.
